title: Fast-path priority coordinator for console event ingress
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Objective:
Build a lightweight, deterministic fast-path priority coordinator that sits in front of the console metrics ingest stream to ensure tenant-critical and SLA-sensitive events are forwarded with bounded latency under load. This component should provide per-tenant priority queuing, token-bucket admission control, and a small hotpath fast-lane that bypasses heavy enrichment for latency-sensitive routes.

Why this ticket:
Our console backend has intermittent tail latency spikes for high-priority customers when bursty workloads and large batches saturate enrichment and downstream processors. Current mitigations (coarse tenant sharding and global backpressure) reduce throughput and increase cost for all customers. A fast-path coordinator will allow us to preferentially route critical events, reduce P99 latency for SLAs, and implement graceful degradation for lower-priority traffic.

Goals / Acceptance criteria:
- Implement a standalone coordinator service (stateless + small local state) that accepts event headers and returns an admission decision (fast-path, normal, shed).
- Per-tenant priority levels (P0/P1/P2) with configurable token-bucket rates and burst sizes via Console feature flags.
- Fast-path events are observed to have 40% lower P99 end-to-end latency in canary tests compared to baseline under the same load profile.
- Coordinator supports idempotent admission tokens (idempotency keys) to avoid double-counting when clients retry.
- Graceful shedding for over-capacity: lower-priority events are dropped or deferred to an economized queue that is processed at lower priority; all drops must emit structured telemetry and a dropped-event reason.
- Compatibility with existing ingress protocols (Kafka and internal HTTP ingestion). Must add minimal extra latency (<2ms median) when not under load.

Design summary (proposed):
- Placement: run as a small fleet in the ingress plane; colocate with edge boxes to avoid extra hop cost. Use consistent hashing by tenant_id to select coordinator instance to maintain local token buckets for hot tenants.
- Admission: token-bucket counters per (tenant, priority). Coordinator responds immediately with a decision and optional short-lived admission token.
- Fast-path: when admitted as fast-path, event bypasses enrichment stage and is routed to a dedicated low-latency pipeline that performs lightweight validation and KV-cache based augmentations.
- Fallbacks: if fast-path pipeline detects schema needs, it can escalate to normal route with transparent backfill.
- Observability: emit admission decisions, queue lengths, token-bucket fill, and per-tenant fast-path QPS metrics to the Console telemetry stream. Provide a Grafana dashboard and alert on sustained >10% drop rate for P0 tenants.

Trade-offs considered:
- Centralized coordinator vs. local per-edge: chose local-per-edge with consistent hashing to avoid single point of failure and reduce hop latency, at the cost of slightly stale token view across edges.
- Strong consistency for token counters vs. eventual: prefer local counters with periodic reconciliation to keep fast-path decisions low-latency.
- Batching token updates vs. immediate: immediate updates for correctness for P0, batching allowed for P2. Configurable by priority.

Implementation plan / tasks:
- Prototype coordinator library (Go) that exposes HTTP admission endpoint and in-memory token buckets. (ENG-974321-1)
- Integrate library into edge ingress binary and run locally in test clusters. (ENG-974321-2)
- Implement fast-path lightweight pipeline consumer that accepts admission tokens and skips enrichment. (ENG-974321-3)
- Add telemetry spans and counters, and a Grafana dashboard skeleton. (ENG-974321-4)
- End-to-end load test harness using k6 + synthetic tenants to validate P99 improvements and drop behavior. (ENG-974321-5)
- Canary rollout: 5% of ingress traffic, pinned by tenant label; monitor drop rates, latency, and error rates for two weeks before progressive expansion. (ENG-974321-6)

Testing matrix:
- Unit tests for token-bucket correctness, idempotency, and consistent-hash routing.
- Integration tests: coordinator + fast-path + normal pipeline interaction.
- Chaos: kill coordinator instances to validate token reconciliation and fallback to normal route without data loss.
- Load tests: simulate bursty tenant patterns, compare p50/p95/p99 for P0 events vs baseline.

Rollout & monitoring:
- Create dashboard showing per-tenant admission decisions, drop rates, token-bucket utilization, and end-to-end latency for fast-path vs normal.
- Alerts: sustained P0 drop rate >5% for >5 minutes; spike in fast-path error rate; token-bucket refill anomalies.
- K8s deployment: two replicas per region for high availability; HPA disabled for predictable behavior.

Security & compliance:
- Admission tokens are ephemeral and signed with runtime KMS; coordinator rotates keys per release.
- Ensure no PII is emitted in telemetry. Review required by Security (ticketing to InfoSec).

Open questions / follow-ups:
- How many priority tiers do we actually need for first release? (P0/P1 only vs P0/P1/P2)
- Fast-path enrichment feature parity: which subset of enrichers are must-haves for canary tenants?
- Rate config surface in Console: should tenant owners be allowed to adjust token rates? (need RBAC guardrails)

Links to artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Fast-Path+Priority+Coordinator
- RFC PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/214
- Prototype branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingress/compare/fastpath-coordinator
- Canary dashboard (WIP): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ingest/fastpath-coordinator-canary

Notes:
Keep implementation incremental: library -> local edge integration -> fast-path consumer -> canary. Focus early on robust observability and safety nets (clear telemetry for drops) before enabling for critical tenants.

2026-03-08 - Tomas Ortega: Prototype admission library implemented (basic token-bucket + idempotency map). Local bench shows median admission latency 0.8ms, p95 1.5ms. Pushed PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingress/pull/542 (WIP).
2026-03-09 - Design review (Aisha Patel): Raised UX question about exposing tenant-level rate config in Console; recommend RBAC + audit log for changes. Added as follow-up work to product backlog.

2026-03-11 - Load test (Tomas): k6 harness simulating 2000 tenants with 5% hot tenants. Under stress, fast-path preserved p99 for P0 down to 180ms vs baseline 320ms. Observed small number of duplicate admissions (edge retries) — added idempotency token TTL to 30s.

2026-03-13 - Tomas Ortega: Open PR for coordinator integration ready for review. Integration tests failing intermittently due to consistent-hash seed mismatch across edge instances; adding deterministic seeding + reconciliation in next patch.
2026-03-14 - Maya Chen: Security review requested (InfoSec ticket INFSEC-2026-77). Scheduling canary for next cycle once seeding issue resolved and Grafana dashboard panels complete.
